scope: One dedicated customer installation/database/server; many organizations and warehouses inside it. No hosted customer registry or routing.
new_forward_profile: Apply unchanged historical hardened-v1.sql, then additive onprem-v1.sql, then onprem-grants.psql; old bindings retain login/kind and signing key FK while org/warehouse columns are removed atomically.

actual_behaviors: Existing first warehouse succeeds but legitimate second warehouse and another organization are omitted from ResolvePrincipal and denied read/write by same store.
Historical warehouse-bound worker leaves second/third warehouse expiry holds and outbox pending.

mutations.name: action
sql_failures: signature binds exact raw argument bytes
signature for read cannot authorize a command

mutations.name: installation
sql_failures: signed context for another installation rejected

retired_mutant.name: worker_scope
retired_mutant.reason: Warehouse-global maintenance within a dedicated client database is the intended on-premise contract. Replaced by worker_fence, which must reject stale leases.

security_properties: Current SQL grants/owner rights gate each request; authenticated identity resolution returns all authorized scopes in this single database.
System actor is rejected even if someone grants it an API permission.
Wrong installation with valid MAC is rejected, including deliberate key reuse.
Replay on another action/backend/transaction or changed raw argument bytes is rejected.
Worker roles check identity then delegate existing global kernels; no maintenance algorithm duplication.
Ping attests cached installation/login and performs signed zero-scope resolve probe so key/identity rotation fails readiness until restored/restarted.
durability_hooks: API transaction uses beginDurableTransaction before context/action
Worker claim/complete/expire use explicit durable transactions and consume/close/error-check rows before COMMIT
remote_apply preserved; weak session defaults strengthened by separately reviewed helper
validation_limits: No claim of production SLA, HA, offsite recovery, or independent adversarial audit completion.
The owning administrator, application signing secret and OIDC verifier remain trusted; a worker credential can service all events in this customer installation.
Single installation UUID must be managed correctly when cloning a database into a new customer deployment.
Full integrated gate/CI and final corruption-flag recovery evidence are root-owned and pending this handoff.
All keys were synthetic in process memory/temporary database; no real credentials or customer data used.
